extractedFacts.wrongfulLockoutCitation: CORRECTED (round-2 research): Cal. Civ. Code Sec. 789.3's $100/day statutory penalty applies, by its own express terms, only to property 'used by a tenant as his or her residence' -- it does not reach commercial tenancies. Commercial self-help lockouts in California are instead governed by the common-law/Code Civ. Proc. Sec. 1159-1161 framework confirmed in Jordan v. Talbot, 55 Cal. 2d 597 (1961): a lease right-of-re-entry clause may be enforced only through judicial process, and a clause purporting to authorize forcible self-help is void as against public policy. That framework yields ACTUAL damages only, not a statutory per-diem penalty.

outcome.description: After a three-day court trial the trial court entered judgment for the landlord on July 3, 2025 awarding possession, $65,989 in past-due rent (the amount demanded in the notice) and $123,111 in holdover damages, $189,100 in total; no fee award is stated in the opinion. The Court of Appeal reversed, holding the three-day notice void because the unpaid rent fell due more than one year before service, and remanded for entry of judgment in favor of the tenant.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed: the three-day notice was void, so the landlord takes nothing in this action.
